denmark/nyhavn-harbour.name: Nyhavn and the Copenhagen harbour
denmark/nyhavn-harbour.description: The colourful 17th-century canal quay with restaurants, plus harbour boat tours.
denmark/nyhavn-harbour.details: Nyhavn is the postcard image of Copenhagen, with painted townhouses and old wooden ships. A canal boat tour passes the Little Mermaid, the Opera House and Christiania. Terraces get busy, so look for quieter lanes just off the quay.

denmark/tivoli-rosenborg.name: Tivoli Gardens and Rosenborg Castle
denmark/tivoli-rosenborg.description: A historic amusement park in the city centre, and a Renaissance castle with the crown jewels.
denmark/tivoli-rosenborg.details: Tivoli opened in 1843 and has rides, gardens and concerts, lit up after dark. Rosenborg Castle, in the King Garden, holds the crown jewels and royal collections. Both are easy to visit on foot from the old town.

denmark/copenhagen-food-design.name: Copenhagen food halls and design
denmark/copenhagen-food-design.description: Smorrebrod, pastries, Torvehallerne market and Danish design shops.
denmark/copenhagen-food-design.details: Copenhagen is a food city, from the open-faced rye sandwiches of smorrebrod to Danish pastry. Torvehallerne market and Reffen street food are good starting points, and the Design Museum shows classic furniture. Cycling is the best way to see the city.

denmark/kronborg-louisiana.name: Kronborg Castle and Louisiana Museum
denmark/kronborg-louisiana.description: Hamlet castle at Helsingor and a modern art museum on the coast, both north of Copenhagen.
denmark/kronborg-louisiana.details: Kronborg is the castle of Shakespeare Hamlet, with ramparts looking across the sound to Sweden. The Louisiana Museum of Modern Art, a short train ride away, has a sculpture park by the sea and a very good cafe. It makes a full-day trip by train.

denmark/roskilde-vikings.name: Roskilde Viking Ship Museum and cathedral
denmark/roskilde-vikings.description: Reconstructed Viking ships by the fjord, and the burial church of the Danish kings.
denmark/roskilde-vikings.details: The Viking Ship Museum displays five ships found in the fjord, and in summer visitors can join a sail. Roskilde Cathedral is a UNESCO site holding royal tombs. Trains from Copenhagen take about 25 minutes.

denmark/odense-andersen.name: Odense and Hans Christian Andersen
denmark/odense-andersen.description: The fairytale author birthplace, with a museum and cobbled lanes of the old town.
denmark/odense-andersen.details: Odense is the capital of Funen. The Hans Christian Andersen Museum tells the story of the writer in a modern space beside his childhood home, and the old streets are lined with colourful houses. The Funen Village open-air museum is nearby. The city is easy to cover on foot.

denmark/aarhus-aros.name: ARoS and the Rainbow Panorama
denmark/aarhus-aros.description: An art museum with a rooftop rainbow walkway and the lively cafes of Denmark second city.
denmark/aarhus-aros.details: ARoS is a large art museum whose roof holds Your Rainbow Panorama, a circular walkway of coloured glass with a city view. The Latin Quarter is full of cafes, and the Aarhus Street Food market offers many cuisines. The Moesgaard Museum shows Viking-age finds.

denmark/den-gamle-by.name: Den Gamle By open-air museum
denmark/den-gamle-by.description: A living museum of historic Danish townhouses, shops and workshops in Aarhus.
denmark/den-gamle-by.details: Den Gamle By is a town of over seventy period buildings brought from across the country, staffed by costumed guides and craftspeople. Seasonal events include a Christmas market. Allow three hours.

denmark/legoland-billund.name: Legoland, Billund
denmark/legoland-billund.description: The original Lego theme park, with Miniland models and family rides.
denmark/legoland-billund.details: Legoland in Billund suits families with rides, Miniland and Lego-brick models of famous places. The nearby LEGO House has a museum and building areas. It opens seasonally, so check dates. Billund has an airport and good bus links.

denmark/skagen-grenen.name: Skagen and Grenen
denmark/skagen-grenen.description: The northern tip of Denmark where two seas meet, and a town of yellow houses and painters.
denmark/skagen-grenen.details: Skagen sits at the end of Jutland, famed for the light that drew a colony of painters. Grenen is a sand spit where the Baltic and North Seas meet, and visitors can stand with a foot in each. The Skagen Museum holds the painters works. Fresh fish is a speciality.

denmark/ribe-wadden.name: Ribe and the Wadden Sea
denmark/ribe-wadden.description: Denmark oldest town, with a cathedral and marshes where tide flats attract birds.
denmark/ribe-wadden.details: Ribe is a medieval town with half-timbered houses and a Romanesque cathedral. The nearby Wadden Sea is a UNESCO site known for tidal flats and bird migrations, with black sun events in spring and autumn. It is a stop on the way between Odense and Jutland.
